chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: The Union board hearing over the Camel job
summary: The black press picked up the story and Lee argued before the union board that he understood his dates, despite his local's president suggesting he was mistaken.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And 47 didn't do anything about it?
Yeah, well, what happened was we took it to Board at 47, because DownBeat made such a big stink about it, and they forced their hands. But now, I had nothing

I don't remember who it was, but he wouldn't go for it, and you know, he said that he was gonna tell DownBeat about it. I don't remember who the trumpet player was at that time, but on the Camel Show -- but he did. And then DownBeat took it, as you can see -- they made quite a splash out of it and it was in all the papers, you know, and then all the black papers picked it up - the Pittsburgh Courier, the Chicago Defender, the Amsterdam News -- they picked it up.

Now that forced us to go to the Union; you know, we had to go before the Board of the Union, so the guy at the Union who was in charge of radio shows and like that, he told his side of it, and he said that he was sure that I had been mistaken; that I had not been hired and that I had just assumed that I had been hired, and this was when the President of the black local -- he was really a nice man, but I ended up calling him an Uncle Tom, because he told them, he said, "You know, Lee is very young, and so maybe he was excited about it and maybe he did misunderstand."

And so I interjected; I said, "Well, you know last week, I had a date at 20th Century Fox, and the same day I had a date ..." I said, "20th Century Fox is out on Peco

Boulevard. I had one at Hal Roach studio on Washington Boulevard in Culver City and I had one in Burbank on the same day. Now, I didn't go to Burbank when I should have been in Culver City, and I didn't go to Culver City when I should have been on Peco, so if I'm intelligent enough to go to the right dates in 3 days -- 3 dates in one day -- I am certain that I understood what CBS told me, and Freddie Fisher told me that I was hired."
Well, everybody's lying and saying that I didn't understand; that I was not hired, and ...
